nodes.label: _detect_face_bbox Function (MediaPipe-first, Haar fallback)
nodes.rationale: MediaPipe face mesh landmarks used first because they handle side-profile photos better than Haar cascade. Haar is only a fallback for frontal faces.

nodes.label: YOLO Face-Crop Strategy (crop to face before detection)
nodes.rationale: YOLO only sees the face region, not hands/hair/background, eliminating false positives. Detection coordinates are offset back to full image space after crop.
nodes.norm_label: yolo face-crop strategy (crop to face before detection)

nodes.norm_label: heatmapoverlay react component with hover tooltips

nodes.label: _build_face_silhouette_mask (MediaPipe 36-point polygon)
nodes.rationale: Eliminates nostril and hairline false positives by using precise MediaPipe face silhouette polygon instead of a bounding box or ellipse.

nodes.label: MediaPipe FaceLandmarker Tasks API
nodes.rationale: mp.solutions.face_mesh was removed in mediapipe 0.10.35 on Python 3.14, causing all face detection to fall through to center-ellipse fallback. The Tasks API (mp.tasks.vision.FaceLandmarker) replaces it with a model-file-based approach that correctly handles side-profile selfies.

nodes.label: Face Silhouette Polygon Mask
nodes.rationale: Using 36 specific MediaPipe landmark indices that trace the exact face boundary instead of rectangular bbox with percentage expansion, to exclude hair at top edges and provide tighter face region for skin analysis.

nodes.label: Nostril Exclusion Mask
nodes.rationale: Dark circular nostril openings match the acne color profile (dark, slightly reddish), causing false positives. Subtracting a nostril polygon (8 landmark indices) from the face silhouette eliminates this source of error.

nodes.label: YOLO Face-Crop-First Detection
nodes.rationale: YOLO running on the full selfie image detects acne-like spots on hands, hair, and background. Cropping to face region first means YOLO physically cannot detect anything outside the face crop.

nodes.label: Per-Condition Composite Heatmap
nodes.rationale: Single green-yellow-red gradient heatmap gives no information about which condition each region represents. Per-condition colors (acne=red, redness=orange, under-eye bags=purple) plus JSON detection metadata allow frontend to render tooltips and drive 3D model vertex coloring.

nodes.label: Face3D Coordinate-Based Vertex Coloring
nodes.rationale: scoreToHeat() zone-based coloring produces unnatural yellow/brown patches unrelated to actual skin tone. Replacing with detection-based coordinate hit-testing against AI output, using median skin tone as base and clinically meaningful condition colors, produces a more accurate diagnostic visualization.

nodes.label: Habit Lock-In UX Pattern
nodes.rationale: Direct checkbox-to-DB write with no confirmation step makes it easy to accidentally log a habit. The Lock In two-step (check → confirm) makes the action deliberate and irreversible, matching the backend's already-irreversible behavior.

nodes.label: Qdrant Activity Log Collection
nodes.rationale: Bloom chatbot needs to accurately retrieve a user's historical skin data. A dedicated 1024-dim bge-m3 embedded collection (skinprogress_activity_log) separate from the 8-dim skinprogress_analyses allows semantic search over natural language event text while preserving exact numeric metadata for filtering.
